Spot premium quotations for imported cathode remained flat and subdued over the past two weeks as the significant negative arbitrage between the SHFE and the LME continued. Traders reported that the latest spot premium quotations for imported cathode and SXEW cathode were between US$30/t and US$50/t, with major traders offering cathode at around US$40-50/t. Very few deals were closed given the persisting RMB3,000/t import loss, and market insiders perceived that most of these deals were cathode imports for financing. Cathode stock is © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **April 2012** www.crugroup.com building up in Shanghai bonded warehouses and re-exporting has been going on since midMarch when the LME moved to backwardation from contango. As a result, cathode inventories increased in the LME Asian warehouses. We were told by market insiders that the cathode inventories in the Shanghai bonded warehouses were still around 550,000t, given the recent inflow and outflow balance. Cathode imports remained at high levels, although a huge SHFE/LME negative arbitrage emerged since the end of January 2012. Jun/09 Dec/09 Jun/10 Dec/10 Jun/11 Dec/11 Data: Chinese Customs data According to the Chinese customs preliminary data, China imported 462,182t of unwrought copper and copper semis in March, down 4.6% m- o-m. We estimate that cathode imports in March registered a slight decline to around 320,000t, thus maintaining a high level and compounding the excess domestic supply. As mentioned in the last publication we believe that the cathode import data for March will be a critical determinant of the short term market sentiment. Market insiders were expecting a more substantial decline and perceive that the continuing hig

h levels of imports may put additional pressure on the market, leading to a gloomier outlook. Despite a significant negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME, cathode imports remained high, as copper continued to be imported to be used as collateral. There are various plays on copper financing. e.g. we heard report that the big traders are making a currency arbitrage play. Moreover, RMB appreciation and importers scheduling more shipments in March before the traditional peak consumption period may also have encouraged the high level of imports. Cathode export data for March has not yet been released. Given that copper smelters are exporting cathode through concentrate tolling business and cathode is being re-exported from Shanghai bonded warehouses, we anticipate that exports may increase to the high levels seen in H1 2011. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **April 2012** www.crugroup.com # Copper substitution in China’s home appliance market According to China's Home Appliance Association’s report, refrigerators, deep freezers and microwave ovens already completed the copper substitution process for major components before 2005. In addition, the refrigeration compressor balance blocks almost completed copper substitution for major components stet 2010. More recently, the high and volatile copper prices have accelerated the research of copper substitution and copper minimization design in the home appliance industry. It is estimated that 10% of air conditioning fan motors and 15%-20% of washing machine motors have used aluminium enameled wire to replace copper enameled wire in 2011. Moreover, refrigerator compressors may begin to use aluminium and copper clad aluminium wire to replace copper wire in 2012. In terms of copper substitution in air conditioners, refrigeration compressors are becoming smaller and more efficient and there is increasing emphasis on copper minimization design. This means that copper consumption intensity in home appliances will continue to decline. In addition, the innovative aluminuim micro channel technology is a strong competitive threat to conventional air conditioner designs. It will use aluminium to totally replace copper and change the inner design of air conditioners. The LME 3-month

copper prices retreated slightly but still traded above $8,000/t, as market sentiment was affected by the re-emerging Eurozone debt concerns and a slowdown in China’s economic growth.  According to NBS data, China’s GDP expanded 8.1% in Q1 2012 y-o-y, the slowest growth in almost three years, after an 8.9% gain in Q4 2011.  IP growth remained stable, fixed asset investment growth y-o-y slowed down but remained at a high level.  China’s

Q1 economic performance is perceived by the market to be disappointing and this may bring downward pressure on copper prices in the short term.  At the same time, extension of credit has increased with new loans in March surging to RMB1.01 trillion.  Buying interest in the copper market increased as the Shanghai physical price declined to below RMB58,000/t.  However, the traditional Q2 demand pick up did not occur and there was a weaker than normal sequential recovery in April.  According to NBS data, China’s refined copper output in March was 510,000t, up 8.5% y-o-y and 16.7% m-o-m, indicating that domestic supply is abundant. The SHFE cathode inventory declined slightly to 221,827t this week but has maintained a high level. We anticipate that the SHFE 3-month copper prices may test the RMB55,000 -56,000/t boundary in the coming two weeks.
